data.head: ## The installed CLI bundles, read as strings (a READING, not a measurement)

body:
Read from `~/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/2.1.328/claude` and `…/2.1.330/claude` with `strings -n 8`, the
window around each name read whole. Minified names differ per version; the shapes below are the same in both.

- **The hard per-call limit.** `di(e)` (2.1.330) / `ii(e)` (2.1.328): the server config's `timeout` when it is a
  number ≥ 1000, else the env `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`, else `1e8` ms (`var km=1e8` / `var Lm=1e8`, 7 368 bytes before
  the function in both bundles), clamped to at least 1000 and at most a module constant (a standalone
  `var au=2147483647;` / `var eu=2147483647;` string stands in each bundle; the binding to the clamp is read by
  name only, unproven). The schema text the CLI ships beside it: «Per-server tool-call timeout in milliseconds.
  Overrides the MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT environment variable for this server. Hard wall-clock limit per call; progress
  notifications do not extend it. Values below 1000ms are ignored (falls through to MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT or the
  default).» The default `1e8` ms is about 27.8 hours.

- **The idle limit.** `Kl(e)` (both): for a `stdio` server `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT` else `1800000` ms
  (30 min); `300000` ms for other remote types; `0` for `sse-ide` / `ws-ide` / `sdk` (an `sdk` server has its own
  arm); `≤ 0` disables; then clamped to at least the per-server `timeout` and at most the hard limit. A 30 s
  watchdog tick aborts the call when no response or progress notification came for that long; a progress
  notification resets the idle clock (`St=Date.now()` in `onprogress`), never the hard limit.

- **At the bound.** The hard limit rejects the one call with an error of class «MCP tool timeout», message
  `MCP server "{server}" tool "{tool}" timed out after {n}s` plus a fixed sentence that the outcome is unknown and
  must be checked before a repeat; the idle abort is «MCP tool idle timeout» with its own message; both carry
  `mcpErrorSource: "downstream_unreachable"`. Nothing read shows the server torn down at either bound — the call
  alone is rejected; a teardown is UNREAD, not read absent.

- **Auto-background.** Both bundles hold `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_AUTO_BACKGROUND_MS`: unset, a gate (`tengu_mcp_auto_background`,
  default true) gives `120000` ms; `sse-ide` / `ws-ide` and an `sdk` server with `disableAutoBackground` are excluded,
  a stdio server is not; a non-interactive session runs it only under `CLAUDE_AUTO_BACKGROUND_TASKS`. Its effect on a
  call past 120 s (the call moved to a background task, the turn going on) is read from the gate's shape only.

- **The 60 s floor.** `ou(e)` (2.1.330) / `Zl(e)` (2.1.328) floors at `60000` ms the per-request timeout of the
  HTTP transports — the only 60 s figure read; it is not the stdio call's limit on these two versions.

- **The names that move it** (names only): the per-server `timeout` key of an MCP server's config; env
  `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_AUTO_BACKGROUND_MS`,
  `CLAUDE_AUTO_BACKGROUND_TASKS`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MCP_TASK_BACKGROUND`; the gate `tengu_mcp_auto_background`.

- **What only a start tells:** that the client applies this bound to a real call of a stdio server as read —
  the error class it returns, the elapsed seconds, whether the server is torn down, and whether a call past 120 s
  in an interactive driver is backgrounded rather than failed.

body:
- **send** — client side: the text checks, the strict-modes and liveness reads, a socket connect, a
  `spawn_blocking` start-time read: unbounded in code, bounded in practice by local file and socket calls. Wrapper
  side: the readiness gate ≤ `GATE_MAX_WAIT` 8.5 s, the flight guard (held by the hook tap's short sections and
  by another send's paste), the paste (no deadline: a 16 MiB text into a child not reading its PTY blocks
  without end), then the window, 10 s or 40 s for `/compact`. The compiled sum is 8.5 + 40 = 48.5 s plus the
  paste; the MCP side waits on the reply with no deadline, so a stalled wrapper holds the call until the
  client's own bound.

- **wait** — `timeout_ms` = min(given, 50 000) (`wait_timeout`, tools.rs:46), run by the wrapper's own clock;
  the MCP side again adds no deadline.
- **last** — one reply read from disk by the wrapper; no wait.

   maps to it (`src/cmd/client.rs` maps its own enum into the set and gains no arm).

2. **The client-bound reading.** `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs` (the only crate that knows Claude) gains
   `MCP_CLIENT_BOUND_READ: Duration` = 120 s, its doc comment saying it is a READING of the 2.1.328 and 2.1.330
   bundles' strings — the auto-background default, the tightest client bound read; the stdio hard limit 1e8 ms and
   the stdio idle limit 1 800 000 ms named beside it as read — never a measurement.

3. **The deadline.** `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs`: `pub const MCP_CALL_DEADLINE: Duration` = 55 s. `frame()`'s
   whole body (the instance check, the liveness read, the socket-directory check, the connect, the peer checks, the
   request and its reply) runs under the deadline: whichever ends first, the frame's result or the deadline, decides;
   at the deadline the result is `result::unreachable(UnreachableCause::CallDeadline)` and the frame's future is
   dropped (its connection closes; the wrapper's own work is not cancelled). The deadline comes from an injected seam
   held by the server: a function giving a future that ends at the deadline — in production Tokio's `sleep` of
   `MCP_CALL_DEADLINE`; in a test a signal the test fires (tests S3: time only through an injected seam, no paused
   Tokio clock). `crates/viola-mcp/src/lib.rs`: `Tools::new` keeps its signature and uses the production seam;
   `Tools::with_deadline(home, own_name, list, deadline)` takes the seam (the handlers suite's door); re-export
   `MCP_CALL_DEADLINE`. `list` is not a frame tool and keeps its 5 s-bounded agents read, unchanged.

4. **Tokio's timer.** `crates/viola-mcp/Cargo.toml`: tokio `features = ["rt", "time"]`. `Cargo.lock` gains no
   package (the feature adds no crate; read `git diff --stat Cargo.lock` after the build: no line). The sole-root
   bans and `scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh` stay green (entries 8, 9).

    the round. A red start is analysed from its ledger line before anything else runs; the spare is spent only on a
    start refused or lost to a cause outside the reading (a host contention, a rig refusal, an account limit) —
    never on a red reading. A fourth base start is the operator's. On an account-limit refusal implement stops where
    it is (`inputs#I2` item 11).

14. After the span: the census keyed `operator`; the ledger's three summaries copied into
    `evidence/live-round.md` (entry 28, report-only), the `outlived` reading among them; entry 27 is the census.
15. The whole integration layer, the smoke, `pre-push`, hygiene, the push and CI (entries 29–36).
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mcpcall.rs` — the stream-json reader into closed words, with its inline cases
- `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs` — `UnreachableCause::CallDeadline` / `call-deadline` and its case row
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs` — `MCP_CLIENT_BOUND_READ`, the reading's constant
- `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs` — `MCP_CALL_DEADLINE`, the deadline over `frame()`, the injected seam, `WAIT_CAP`'s comment, the bound's unit case
- `crates/viola-mcp/src/lib.rs` — `Tools::with_deadline`, the re-export
- `crates/viola-mcp/src/result.rs` — the cause table case gains `CallDeadline`
- `crates/viola-mcp/Cargo.toml` — tokio's `time` feature
- `crates/viola-mcp/tests/handlers.rs` — the held reply, the two deadline cases
- `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` — the new writer named, if the census asks
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs` — `Arm::MB`, its labels, `Plan.fake`, the arm, the table cases
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs` — `--fake`, the labels in the doc
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs` — the `MB` rehearsals

The block runs: phase A (formatter, linter, the three crates' units, the viola-mcp suite, the call-deadline control's
filtered entry, the error-bodies census, the tokio and rmcp gates); phase B (the rig library cases, the `MB`
rehearsals through the integration layer, which builds the root binaries they spawn); the round (entries 14–26,
`round` and `live` entries ONLY, `inputs#I2` item 10), its after-reads of state other actors move keyed to the
round; after the span the census keyed `operator` and the report-only ledger read; then the whole layers and the
operator pass. What is not run, and why: no mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 10); no release-check entry (CI's
`release` job runs it); `cargo deny check` is CI's `supply-chain` job (no dependency is added, a feature only; the
tokio bans are entries 8–9). Every test start runs under a test-owned home; every waiting test takes a bound under
the 20 s lint, the handlers' held reply a 5 s backstop. The live starts run under the rig's private scratch and
config; the rig's `--deadline` bounds each under its entry's `timeout`. The non-priming probes of each live leg are
the round entries ahead of it. The whole-round dry-run is shown on the P5 card.
**The remove-the-guard control** is implement's one-shot `gate.py control`, never an entry:
| | `call-deadline` |
| **File** | `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs` |
| **The edit removes** | the deadline over `frame()`: the frame awaited alone, the seam's future never polled |
| **Case** | `handlers_frame_tools_end_at_the_call_deadline::case_1_send` |
| **Fired on** | entry 6, `--timeout 300` |

With the guard removed the call returns the canned reply at the wrapper's 5 s backstop, the case reads its detail
red, and no `TIMEOUT` line can stand for it (300 s against a 5 s backstop); a `timeout` reading would NOT read the
guard as held. The filter selects 0 tests on the untouched tree and the four cases once they exist.

title: 2026-11-21-mcp-calls-bounded — 1. Test Scope Summary: 1 row(s)
body:
## 2026-11-21-mcp-calls-bounded — 1. Test Scope Summary: 1 row(s)
**Section:** 1. Test Scope Summary
**Change:** ~ decision/cli-mcp-identical-payloads · except: was «»; now «call-deadline, written by the MCP frame tools alone, has no CLI document.»
**Why:** decision/cli-mcp-identical-payloads: The standing rule is false for the one MCP-only cause word; the exception names that member, without the member counts fit read as an inventory.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-21T22-34-30Z-wrap/

- Every time bound viola holds (wait timeout and cap, MCP call deadline, dialog hold, send readiness gate, confirmation windows, agents read, the start's Claude config lock wait) falls on the driver, viola's child or viola's own start; no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it. An MCP frame tool call (send, wait, last, answer) that outlives the MCP call deadline (55 s) ends `instance-unreachable` / `call-deadline`, the outcome of a send unknown; only the MCP frame tools write that detail, never the CLI, whose exit-21 cause set stays six. The one `claude agents --json` read `viola list` and `viola revive` each make (chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board) is killed at 5 s, a bound on viola's own child only: a failed, oversize, malformed or timed-out read fails open, and no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it. `viola wait` returns `{timed_out:true}` only for a timeout the caller passes in. The MCP `wait` tool (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers) clamps its `timeout_ms` to `WAIT_CAP` 50 000 ms, also its default when the caller passes none (`viola_mcp::wait_timeout`), so an MCP `wait` with no timeout is answered `timed-out` after 50 s: a bound on the driver only (the hidden, plugin-run `viola mcp` serves a driving Claude session, never a person), no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it, and the wheel is untouched. A raised dialog takes a `viola answer` only within the dialog hold (`config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s`, whole seconds 60–3600, default 60, PROVISIONAL bounds; chunk 2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver); at the hold's end the wrapper replies `null` and appends one `dialog-expired` line, the dialog renders for the human in the `claude` TUI, and a later `answer` for it is refused `not-delivered` / `unknown-dialog` (exit 13) — the hold bounds the driver, never the human: any human key still hands the held dialog back at once, whatever the hold. A `viola send` on a verified CLI waits in the readiness gate for at most `GATE_MAX_WAIT` (8.5 s) and is then refused `not-delivered` / `input-not-ready` with nothing typed; a key pressed during the wait goes to the child and takes the wheel at once, and the waiting send is then refused `human-typing`. Once typed, a confirmed `viola send` waits for its confirmation within `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK` (10 s), and a `/compact` send on a verified CLI within its own `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` (40 s, PROVISIONAL, architecture [Delivery Confirmation]); a send not confirmed inside its window is `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted`: a bound on the driver only, the confirm wait takes no key and blocks, refuses or delays none, and the wheel is untouched.

The shared vocabulary of every other crate: the normalised event kinds, `RefusalReason` and its closed detail sets (`HumanTyping { ManualPause }` among them), `TurnEndCause` (the closed cause set of `turn-ended`, nine words `rate-limited` · `overloaded` · `auth-failed` · `billing` · `invalid-request` · `model-not-found` · `server-error` · `output-limit` · `api-error`, no Claude-specific name), `UnreachableCause` (`StrictModes` · `InstanceDead` · `UnwrappedName` · `EndpointLost` · `ServerVerify` · `SocketDir` · `CallDeadline`, each word through `as_str`, `SocketDir`'s `socket-dir-refused`, `CallDeadline`'s `call-deadline`: a closed set of seven, with no serde path and no `RefusalReason`; the first six are exit 21's, written by both clients, `call-deadline` by the MCP frame tools alone), the wheel's `WheelCause` (`start` · `human-input` · `manual-pause` · `release`), the nutype newtypes `ViolaName` and `DialogHold` (whole seconds 60–3600), the protocol `v` constants, the shared validators (`validate_paste_text`, and `is_code_word`: 1 to 64 bytes of `[a-z0-9-]`, a lower-case letter first), the `MAX_FRAME` constant (16 MiB), `SPINE_DEADLINE` (1 s, the spine bound the perf gate reads), `DIALOG_HOLD_DEFAULT` · `DIALOG_HOLD_MIN` · `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX` (60 s · 60 s · 3600 s: the dialog hold's default and bounds, `config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s` read once at the wrapper's start into a `DialogHold`; the hook bounds its reply read at `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX + 5 s`, below the `hooks.json` `timeout` of 3615), the injected `Clock` seam (`SystemClock` in production; first consumer `run`'s vt100 feed thread), `SERVICE_NAME` / `VERSION`, and the obs vocabulary (`obs_event!`, `ObsEvent`, `ObsProcess`). It performs no I/O and depends on no viola crate. It does NOT know Claude payload shapes (that is `viola-agent-claude`), and it does not depend on `tracing`: `obs_event!` expands to `::tracing::event!` at the caller.

- Success = `isError:false` + the channel `ok` payload as `structuredContent`; refusal = `isError:true` + `{refusal, detail}` + text `refused: <reason>` (a peer's `refusal` that is no code word reads `unknown`, a string `detail` that is no code word `null`, and a non-string `detail` no known reply); unreachable / fault = `isError:true` + `{"error":"instance-unreachable"|"wrapper-fault","detail":…}` (`instance-unreachable` with `detail` its cause word, built by `result::unreachable(cause)` from a `viola_core::UnreachableCause`: `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed` · `socket-dir-refused` · `call-deadline` (MCP's alone, the 55 s call deadline's expiry), `of_reply` reading `Connect` as `InstanceDead` and `Closed | Io` as `EndpointLost`, `of_board` the board's refusal as `StrictModes`, and `tools.rs` `frame` no `live_endpoint` through `viola_state::liveness::without_endpoint`, a refused `viola_state::strict::check_endpoint_dir` after `live_endpoint` as `SocketDir` and a refused `peer_admitted(client.server_euid())` or a failed `server_verified` as `ServerVerify`, each with no frame and no line, `isError` the record; `wrapper-fault` with the JSON-RPC fault's `{code,message,data}` as `viola_channel::sanitised_fault` reads it: a fixed `message`, `data` a closed object or null); a frame tool (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`) first runs `viola_state::strict::check_instance` on the home and the target instance, before `live_endpoint` (a refusal returns the `instance-unreachable` result with `detail: "strict-modes-failed"`, text `refused: instance-unreachable`, and writes no frame and no line); a frame tool whose connected server is not the recorded wrapper (on Unix its peer euid not this user's or unreadable, `peer_admitted`; else its peer pid or OS start time not the snapshot's, or the check cannot be made; either reads `UnreachableCause::ServerVerify`; the start time read on `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`) returns the `instance-unreachable` result with `detail: "server-verify-failed"`, no frame written and no log line. Every `isError` text is `refused: <code>`, and every MCP error result carries codes and fixed messages only, no path and no upstream text, each body a row of `MCP_RESULTS` in `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs`. JSON-RPC errors are the MCP connection's own faults, an unknown tool name (`-32602`) and an internal handler fault (any other channel error, a reply of no known shape, a `wait` / `last` refusal, a panicked call), which is `-32603` `internal error` with `data: null`.

- MCP `wait` sends `timeout_ms` = `min(given, 50 000)` (`viola_mcp::WAIT_CAP`, `wait_timeout`), 50 000 ms when none is given, and `after` as given: below the 55 s MCP call deadline, itself below the client's tool-call bound, so a wait returns before either cuts the call. Every frame tool call (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`; `list` is not under it) is bounded by that compiled 55 s call deadline: at expiry the call's work is dropped and the tool returns `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `call-deadline`.

- CLI exit codes: 0 · 1 (a `cli` verb's internal error: `error: internal error` on stderr, or under `--json` before a `--` the catch site's `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` on stdout, stderr then empty, `run`, `revive`'s start, `mcp` and `hook` silent at that site; also `viola run`'s and `viola revive`'s start, and `viola verify`, refusing the home tree before any log opens: the home-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or the instance-state pair for an instance-level refusal, no line written, no child started; also `viola run` and `viola revive`'s start refusing the socket directory (`socket_dir_ready`, before any snapshot, child or `Server::bind`; a failed create and a refused check read this one code, a `Server::bind` failure does not): the stderr `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or under `viola revive --json` the `socket-dir-refused` document, and one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"socket-dir-refused"}`, no path, pid or uid; `viola verify`'s refusals each carry their code on the `process-exit` it writes under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME`: `program-not-found` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `version-unreadable` · `strict-modes-failed` · `unclean-fixture`, beside `interrupted`; a failing row is no refusal and carries no code, yet `viola verify` still exits 1 on a failed relied row with that row's stamp written, and `verify` takes no `--json`) · 2 (usage error, and `viola send` text over 16 MiB or not UTF-8) · 10 human-typing · 11 unassigned (the retired `budget-paused` refusal's code, never reused or renumbered) · 12 unverified-cli · 13 not-delivered · 14 unknown · 20 wrapper fault (a `-32602` from `link` / `unlink` included) · 21 instance unreachable (under `--json` `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"<cause>"}`, written by `client::unreachable_document` (the board builds its own), `<cause>` one of the six exit-21 words of `viola_core::UnreachableCause`'s closed seven (the seventh, `call-deadline`, written by the MCP frame tools alone) `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed` · `socket-dir-refused`, no `RefusalReason`; with no live endpoint `viola_state::liveness::without_endpoint` reads an instance directory as `instance-dead` and anything else as `unwrapped-name`, so a stale instance reads `instance-dead`, and a wrapper lost with the call open reads `endpoint-lost`; also, on `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` / `link` / `unlink`, a server that is not the recorded wrapper — a connected peer whose euid is not this user's or cannot be read (`peer_admitted`), or the connected peer's pid or OS start time not the snapshot's, or that check not made — no frame written, `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"server-verify-failed"}` under `--json` (Linux only; the Windows and macOS legs left with their code, recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final`), after the client's own exit-13 refusals, the strict-modes instance check and the socket-directory check, with no exit code or `RefusalReason` of its own, its `--json` word the document's `detail`; also `viola list`'s refused strict-modes check of the home, `instances/` or any one instance, which refuses the whole board, no log opened; and `viola plugin install`'s refused strict-modes check of the home or an existing `marketplace/` tree dir, nothing created, no log opened; and the refused instance check of `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` (the target instance) and of `viola link` / `viola unlink` (the driven instance), made first by `client::refuse_untrusted` (`check_instance` on the home and `instances/<name>`, after `send`'s text read, before any connect, role file or log opens): the instance-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}` under `--json`, no log opened, no line written; and, on those same eight verbs, past that check and before any connect, a refused socket directory on the recorded endpoint (`check_endpoint_dir` in `client::connect`): the socket-directory hint last on stderr, or `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"socket-dir-refused"}` under `--json`, one `process-exit` at WARN with `during` `connect` and no `channel-request`);
